newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Heat build spoils API report's bullishness.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Heat build spoils API report's bullishness.

text.p: REUTER SURVEY ESTIMATES* ACTUAL STOCKS FOR
FOR WEEK ENDED 06/27/97 WEEK ENDED 06/20/97-CHANGE
DISTILLATE...... UP 2.00 116,648 UP 4.023 MLN
UTILIZATION..... DN 0.50 96.9 DN 0.7 PCT PT
*NB - The survey estimate is derived by omitting the high
and low forecast and averaging the rest, with a sample of at
least six.

A sharp crude stock drop, a healthy gasoline draw but a surprisingly robust jump in heating oil stocks gave this week's report American Petroleum Institute (API) report a decidedly mixed flavor, traders said.
Still, many players downplayed the apparently bearish distillate build and focused instead on the more bullish drops last week of crude and especially gasoline stocks.

"It looks like gasoline will be the dominant leader in the market," said Richard Redash, an energy analyst at Prudential Securities. "The gasoline number was more bullish than crude and with gasoline's recent uptrend it will take the lead."
The API said gasoline stocks fell by 1.23 million barrels to 204.2 million -- helped by declines in output and imports as well as continued solid demand.

The decline in output to just shy of 8.1 million barrels per day (bpd) was largely the result of a 0.7 percentage point drop in refinery utilization that brought run rates to 96.9 percent of total capacity.
Gasoline imports abated to 298,000 bpd from the prior week's 583,000 bpd, while implied demand stayed at a rather robust 8.57 million barrels per day.
The crude drop also captured the market's attention, especially in the first moments following the report's release.

"The market is definitely short crude with the Iraq thing," said one trader, referring to delays in resumption of the UN-Iraq oil-for-food deal, the humanitarian exception to UN sanctions on Iraq after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
API said crude stocks dropped by 4.36 million barrels to just under 318 million barrels.

But some players were quick to note that on the West Coast, crude stocks dropped by 3.75 million barrels while only by 1.2 million on the Gulf Coast, home of the biggest concentration of oil refineries on the planet.
Crude imports, including those from Canada, meanwhile rose by 571,000 bpd to 8.83 million bpd, the API report said.

Regarding the 4.02 million barrel build in distillate stocks that brought inventories to 116.6 million barrels or 16.9 million over year-ago levels, traders saw bearishness tempered by the seasonal tendencies of distillates to build.
"I don't think distillates are the trump card," said one trader, noting that even if the build exceeded expectations, distillates should be building at this time of year.
But in ACCESS trade heating oil was moving the most, with the August contract down by about 0.25 cent from the earlier NYMEX close of 54.84.

Crude oil was also dipping by early evening after getting a bullish jolt immediately after API's report came out, with the August contract bid 9 cents below the earlier NYMEX settlement of $20.12 a barrel.
August gasoline was about steady in ACCESS trade with the earlier settlement of 58.78 cents a gallon.
-- New York Oil Desk +1 212 859 1633
